i view alcoholics as someone who consistantly abuses the substance or is straight up addicted . as someone who has ran substance abuse treatment groups in the past , here is how abuse is typically defined : abuse of any substance is when you use a substance in such a manner that it * * often * * negatively impacts certain aspects of your life . these aspects include : * relationships ( family / friends / spouses ) * legal ( e . g . dwi ' s / public intoxication ) * work and / or school ( calling out of work / poor grades ) * medical ( mental and / or physical ) * financially now addiction is much deeper problem . the user at this point has built a dependence upon the substance , be it mentally , physically , or both . keep in mind , i ' m not saying someone that calls out of work twice a year because they ' re too hungover is an alcoholic . i ' m classifying alcoholics as someone who habitually abuses or has become addicted to the substance . this is how a measure the line and whether or not i have crossed it . if i do cross it , i will cut back my use or stop completely . until then , cheers !

this man gets it ! yeah , back when i was dealing with clinical depression ( it was actually diagnosed as dysthymia by my psychologist , ) a few beers would help me be at my best and actually got me out of my social anxiety and , in a bizarre but completely obvious way , taught me how to socialize . before this school year , when i started to actually drink more than once every few months ( and even then , i only started drinking my first year of college , which was the year before , ) i basically had no friends and didn ' t know how to socialize . booze didn ' t really * make * me good at socialization as much as it unlocked a part of me that was already there to begin with , and a part of me that i ' ve now learned how to unlock even while sober . the result ? happier than i ' ve ever been in my entire life - - not so much because i have friends , but because i ' ve realized that there are , in fact , things about me that people like , and that i ought to like those things too , because they ' re demonstrably good things about myself . also , just to clarify ( so i ' m not liable in case anyone gets it wrong ) : there are * some * subtleties to " excess in moderation . " basically , the idea is that a little bit of excessive drinking isn ' t so bad , but that 1 ) there should be limits , even when you do drink to excess , and 2 ) that you don ' t want to drink to excess every night . the reason for the first is that pushing yourself beyond your limits too many times can cause permanent damage - - and , in fact , pushing yourself beyond your limits just * once * can sometimes cause permanent damage . if your limit is sixteen drinks in a night , but you still feel great after twelve , you don ' t need to push yourself to hit sixteen plus if you ' re already feeling wonderful . the reason for the second is that , if you have responsibilities to keep track of and want to make sure you can fulfill those responsibilities , drinking to excess every night is a terrible idea . and if you don ' t have responsibilities , either you ' re doing something right or you ' re doing something terribly wrong , and you should examine your life beyond whether or not you drink too much . " excess in moderation " really is key - - and it applies to things other than drinking . i love coca - cola , but if i had twenty cans of coke a day , i ' d get very fat very quickly , and i ' d soon run out of money . i love working out , but if i lifted weights every day of the week i ' d first of all not see results ( because you need a rest period of somewhere in the neighborhood of forty - eight hours , ) and second of all in all likelihood i ' d damage my health through overtraining at some point . i love smoking cigarettes , but i restrict my smoking habits ( and in all likelihood i should probably not smoke at all , but i ' m still young and my body can repair itself quickly , ) and i ' ve promised myself i ' ll quit when i hit twenty - one - - although whether or not i ' ll actually follow through remains to be seen . i love smoking cigars too , but if i smoked cigars every day i ' d be one sick motherfucker and my wallet would be a lot lighter . i love eating hot wings , but if i ate hot wings for every meal my stomach would * not * like me - - nor would my rectum , although nobody needs to know about that . it ' s because of this that i drink very little coke , despite how much i love it . it ' s why i only lift three times a week . it ' s why i don ' t smoke a pack a day . it ' s why i only buy a cigar less frequently than once a month . it ' s why i don ' t eat hot wings for every meal . . . although come to think of it , hot wings are probably my biggest vice , and at the moment i ' d * love * to have hot wings for every meal , but i don ' t because i know it would catch up with me . that way , yes , everything is still in moderation , but you can still do your favorite things to excess as long as you moderate how often and how much . so again : 1 ) set definite limits when you exploit your vices to excess ( i . e . go near your limit , but never to or over ) 2 ) moderate the frequency to which you exploit your vices to excess ( i . e . don ' t _ _ _ _ _ _ _ to excess every single day , or it ' ll come back to bite you in the ass . )

cliff from cheers has this bit of wisdom to share , “well , you see , norm , it’s like this . a herd of buffalo can only move as fast as the slowest buffalo . and when the herd is hunted , it’s the slowest and weakest ones at the back that are killed first . this natural selection is good for the herd as a whole , because the general speed and health of the whole group keeps improving by the regular killing of the weakest members . in much the same way , the human brain can only operate as fast as the slowest brain cells . now , as we know , excessive intake of alcohol kills brain cells . but naturally , it attacks the slowest and weakest brain cells first . in this way , regular consumption of beer eliminates the weaker brain cells , making the brain a faster and more efficient machine . and that , norm , is why you always feel smarter after a few beers . ”

i equate it to a habitual weed smoker . i feel they do it because they like the way it makes them feel , the atmosphere of the buzz , and because they enjoy it . there is no problem with drinking alcohol to feel those same feelings . at the same time , if alcohol is " your poison " so to speak , you have to realize it has an incredibly higher potential for abuse , and with that abuse comes a much harsher effect on your body and well being . if you can strike a happy balance and are able to enjoy some drinks to chill out and make you feel better , go for it . but when you start slamming 12 - 18 beers a night , and when you ' re sober you just can ' t wait til the day is over to repeat the cycle , that ' s when you should analyze and potentially recognize that the habit is problematic .

& gt ; _ _ alcohol withdrawal syndrome _ _ is a set of symptoms that can occur when an individual reduces or stops alcoholic consumption after long periods of use . prolonged and excessive use of alcohol leads to [ tolerance ] ( http : / / en . wikipedia . org / wiki / drug _ tolerance ) and [ physical dependence ] ( http : / / en . wikipedia . org / wiki / physical _ dependence ) . the withdrawal syndrome is largely a hyper - excitable response of the [ central nervous system ] ( http : / / en . wikipedia . org / wiki / central _ nervous _ system ) to lack of alcohol . symptoms typical of withdrawal include agitation , [ seizures ] ( http : / / en . wikipedia . org / wiki / seizure ) , and [ delirium tremens ] ( http : / / en . wikipedia . org / wiki / delirium _ tremens ) . & gt ; [ sedative - hypnotics ] ( http : / / en . wikipedia . org / wiki / sedative ) , such as alcohol , are well known for their propensity to induce [ physiological dependence ] ( http : / / en . wikipedia . org / wiki / physiological _ dependence ) . this dependence is due to alcohol - induced neuro - adaptation . withdrawal is characterized by neuropsychiatric excitability and autonomic disturbances . dependence on other sedative - hypnotics can increase the severity of the withdrawal syndrome . & gt ; elimination of large concentrations of alcohol from the blood is an example of 0 order kinetics , that is , the concentration , which is the bac does not change the rate at which the alcohol is eliminated . therefore the quantity you are interested in is probably the area under the curve which would reflect the amount of alcohol you have drunk and is best reflected by number of standardized drinks . that being said bac is an important marker for the toxic thresholds of alcohol , such as stopping breathing . tl ; dr : long term damage is defined by number of drinks , short term problems are defined by bac .

good rules of thumb that will help you to avoid being an alkie with liver damage : 1 . don ' t drink before the sun sets . it wont kill you to drink a beer or two at a sunday bar - b - que or whatever , but lunchtime ( or worse , morningtime ) drinking is a big step down a slippery slope . hair of the dog works all too well , it can become kinda insidious . 2 . don ' t drink 2 days in a row . again , it won ' t kill you to do it every once in a while . and to be honest , more than the other rules of thumb mentioned here , this is something that a fair few people do anyway , to moderation , without any liver damage ( example : france ) that said , drinking daily is the * textbook way * of becoming an alcoholic . getting the ch3ch2oh out of your bloodstream completely before adding it in again helps avoid physical addiction , which is a real thing for satan ' s piss aka alcohol 3 . don ' t drink alone . yet again , having a beer on your own after work in front of the tv isn ' t as bad as shooting heroin or something . but . it ' s not something you want to get into the habit of . and , alcohol is a tricky devil that likes to sneakily get you into the habit of imbibing . so - don ' t drink alone on any sort of regular basis . 4 . 2 or 3 drinks at a time is where regular people with a job in the morning tend to stop . if it takes you 4 drinks just to start getting your buzz on , it ' s time to take a break for a month or two , till 2 beers starts making you feel a lil sloshed and happy again . 5 . blackouts are a * huge * red flag ! you kinda get a pass if it happens like once or twice when you ' re in uni and stuff , but more than twice , or after you ' ve graduated : again , a slippery slope that leads nowhere good . 6 . speaking of slippery slopes - booze can be pretty damn slippery and slopey and stuff . sneaky . seductive even . you start at 3 drinks a day , but all your friends are sucking down 5 or 6 after work and you don ' t want to look like a pussy . even though it ' s thursday , and you ' ve been out with your buddies every day this week already . or . you come home on a tuesday , there ' s 4 beers in the fridge . you ' re on your own , but it was a tough day at work . 1 loner beer turns into 2 . turns into 4 . turns into a walk to the corner store , and 6 . a few too many maybe , but your tv show was extra funny that night , and you ' re not even hung over in the morning . then , hey ! what do you know , there ' s 4 left in the fridge when you get home from work the next day ! none of the above really needs to be a problem if it ' s just a few times . but rinse and repeat for 5 years ? . . . alcohol is physically and mentally addicting . for most people it ' s no big deal , but here you are , asking the internet cause you ' re a little worried for some reason . seriously , for most people it ' s fine , but for some it can in fact ruin your health , marriage , job , life . since you ' re asking , keep an eye on it - alcoholism is a real thing , and all too common . all that said , to be honest you don ' t really sound so different from every other red blooded ' merkin college kid ever . no need to freak out about the booze - a - hol just now , you ' re probably fine . relax , for 99 people out of 100 , a few brewskis are just a fun way to loosen up a bit on the weekend ! that said , the above rules of thumb are pretty widely accepted as normal - people ways to not turn into an alkie later on down the road

fermentation of drinkables generate mostly ethanol but small amounts of methanol . good vodkas have virtually none , cheap red wine has a much larger amount proportionately , bad moonshine can have enough to kill , and does ( recently killed [ 120 in india ] ( http : / / www . cleveland . com / world / index . ssf / 2011 / 12 / india _ probes _ scores _ of _ deaths . html ) ) . methylated spirits is 95 % ethyl acohol with 5 % methyl added to stop people drinking it . ok , so your body has a preference for processing ethyl over methyl alcohol , so consuming lots it won ' t process the methyl until it gets thru the ethyl . ethanol breaks down thru a number of steps into carbon dioxide and water . methanol breaks down to a nasty acid and base . this is what causes hangovers . when you wake up still drunk your body hasn ' t finished processing the ethanol . once it does it starts on the methanol and your hangover fades in . this ois also why ' hair of the dog ' works . stick more ethanol in yr system , it staves off the methanol processing ( best dealt with while you ' re asleep ) . i stick to good beer anyway , haven ' t had a hangover in years . that was somewhat simplified , but i never meant to type so much anyway . but now u know .

when you ' re home , alone , and on vacation , you aren ' t doing it right if your first drink upon waking up is * not * alcoholic .
* alcohol causes your body to produce more urine . in turn , urinating more than usual can lead to dehydration — often indicated by thirst , dizziness and lightheadedness . * alcohol triggers an inflammatory response from your immune system . your immune system may trigger certain agents that commonly produce physical symptoms , such as an inability to concentrate , memory problems , decreased appetite and loss of interest in usual activities . * alcohol irritates the lining of your stomach . alcohol increases the production of stomach acid and delays stomach emptying . any of these factors can cause abdominal pain , nausea or vomiting . * alcohol can cause your blood sugar to fall . if your blood sugar dips too low , you may experience fatigue , weakness , shakiness , mood disturbances and even seizures . * alcohol causes your blood vessels to expand , which can lead to headaches . * alcohol can make you sleepy , but your quality of sleep will decrease . this may leave you groggy and tired . * alcoholic beverages contain ingredients called congeners , which give many types of alcoholic beverages their flavor and can contribute to hangovers . congeners are found in larger amounts in dark liquors , such as brandy and whiskey , than in clear liquors , such as vodka and gin .

you would need to calculate the free water in the alcohol you are drinking ( essential 100 % - abv % ) * amount of alcoholic beverage . then you need to have some sort of measuring device for your urine . subtract the free water volume of the alcohol from the amount of urine . whatever that number is you should drink at least that much in water or , even better , of an isotonic drink like gatorade or pedialyte . however , the alcohol is going to have a dehydrating effect overnight , so you should drink maybe an extra ~ 30 ounces or so of water / isotonic drink on top of that . this will not entirely prevent a hangover , because dehydration is probably not the only thing that causes the hangover symptoms , but at least you wont ' t be hungover and dehydrated .

right , i see what you ' re saying . i guess if i were introducing someone to alcohol , i ' d try to find a good balance between taste / drinkability and proof / abv . liquor [ yknow , regular , 80 proof / 40 % booze ] doesn ' t require a lot of liquid to get drunk , but it ' s so abrasive on the tongue and throat that i couldn ' t recommend it to someone alcohol naiive . as for wine , even if you get the kinda stuff you describe , you ' ll still need to drink an entire bottle of it to get two drinks into you . that ' s a lot of liquid , and it ' s going to be very filling . it ' s not just the abv i ' m concerned with ; just having lots of liquid sitting in your stomach increases the likelihood of getting sick . i maintain beer is the best way to go . you can drink it and keep it down , it ' s not super - abrasive to the tongue like liquor , and you only need to drink say , 24 ounces of liquid to get the same amount of alcohol that the wine you describe would deliver . so in case that didn ' t make any sense whatsoever , here ' s what i ' m trying to say : * getting sick / too drunk can be caused by a combination of the strength of the drink , * as well as * how much liquid you consume . hell , if you drink a gallon of even water too quickly , you ' re not gonna have a happy stomach . * liquor : while it doesn ' t fill up your stomach the way beer or wine does , it ' s just too abrasive for a new - drinker to drink a lot of . * wine [ for the sake of the example , lets say its a 750ml bottle , but so weak that it only contains 2 standard drinks ] : it ' ll taste fine , the drinker will barely notice the alcohol , but it ' ll require so much liquid to get you feeling it that you still might end up sick , just from all that wine sitting in your stomach . * beer [ just regular beer ] : is stronger than the aforementioned weak wine , so you don ' t need to drink as much to have a similar effect , but the taste isn ' t nearly as harsh as 80 proof liquor . it ' s a nice middle ground in this case . however , if the wine we ' re talking about is regular 24 proof wine say , that might be a better way to go , since you won ' t need to drink as much as you would beer , but it ' s not so harsh going down the way liquor is .

i ' ve also used scotch rocks , but i ' m not a big fan , they ' re kind of a gray area that i don ' t really need . if it ' s a good single malt scotch , i ' ll usually just drink it neat . i used to ice a lot more scotches , but the alcohol burn doesn ' t bother me anymore so i don ' t really * need * the ice or water . when you cool ethanol , the volatility goes down so you don ' t get all the aromas you normally would if it were room temperature . if the aromas are good , i want em , if they ' re harsh , i cool it down a bit . now something like a bourbon , i ' ll usually ice . the aromas and the flavors of it can be a bit harsh for me sometimes so i find i ' m able to enjoy them more if the edge is taken off by a little melting ice . the scotch rocks don ' t really cool the drink off enough / for long enough to make a legitimate impact on the drink ( in my opinion at least ) , and the lack of a splash of water is a negative for me . pretty much my standard is as follows : * if it ' s a spirit that i ' d normally mix to improve the flavor ( bourbon for a manhattan , vodka , etc ) , i ' ll usually drink it on a little ice if i ' m having it straight . * if it ' s a spirit that i ' d never mix ( good , high quality whiskeys ) , i want it neat . * the only exception to both for me is irish whiskey , because i don ' t mix it but i like it chilled and thinned a bit . tl ; dr : if i want it cold , i probably want it thinned out a bit too . if i don ' t want it thinned out , i probably don ' t want it cold either .

tl ; dr lol not gonna happen ok . i ' m pretty drunk right now and i know that people are gonna downvote me for this , but i . d . c , this is a throw - away acc . i know this may seem a bit off topic , but here it goes . you know how eventually either you or others can smell the alcohol on your breath ? ' cause that ' s how you get caught . although some drugs cannot be detected by breath tests , it must be able to enter your bloodstream to have any effect on your bodily functions in general , for anyone to gain any sort of effect from any type of drug , it must enter their vascular system . i ' m pretty sure that you know that our bodies have hundreds / thousands of miles of blood vessels throughout our body , and one of the most densely packed areas of blood vessels to surface area ratio is our lungs . without a high density of capillaries to s . a , it would be very difficult to absorb oxygen into our bodies . one key fact of absorbing oxygen is that there is a very , very thin layer of cells capable of exchanging co2 for o2 . side note : the average body temp of a human is 36 . 8 c ( 98 . 6 f ) . ethanol ( c2h6o , commonly refered to as alcohol ) vaporizes at around 28 . 7 c ( 78 . 3 f ) . the fact that alcohol vaporizes at a lower temp . than our own body temp . ( although not by much ) is hot enough to allow the vapors to pass through the alveoli / cells / capillaries of our lungs and out into the surrounding atmosphere , which obviously allows for anyone within the general vicinity of your breath to be able to notice the alcohol . no matter how you ingest / consume the alcohol ( via ingestion , i . v . , up your butt , etc . ) it can and will be able to pass through your lungs and create a noticable smell , no matter how hard you try to cover it up . i ' d like you to look upon an old episode of mythbusters where they tried various methods of covering up alcohol on a breathalyzer test . none of them worked . another tl ; dr : if you eventually do figure out how to get drunk without it being detected , i suggest that you publish it to a recognizable and notable journal , have the experiment peer reviewed hundred / thousands of times , and then collect your nobel prize . source : chemistry major with a minor in biochemistry and fermentation sciences edit : i ' m very drunk right now , so o . p , if my original comment was shorter than this one , it is because i am drunk , and cannot type correctly . praise jeeebus for google and it ' s autocorrect . edit 2 : i swear , i can type out more scientific facts / papers / whatever better drunk than sober . maybe i should create another alt . acc . called drunk _ chemist .

preface : i am playing it fast and loose here , but i am drunk , so i beg that be forgiven . there is something deep within structure of those self - regulating dynamical systems that manage to remain relatively stable over periods of time , that keeps them stable ( well , at least over short periods of time ) . we are such systems . by definition , that regulating thing is homoeostasis . our bodies regulate their temperatures to keep our cells working . our brains regulate their levels of neuro - chemicals to keep us driven and reproducing ( and alive ) . when we experience a new stimulus , our brains reacts strongly . in the case of booze , this is pleasurable . over time , the brain adjusts and this becomes the new normal . something about dopamine . anyway , it has to be this way . imagine the alternatives ? 1 . our brains release pleasure chemicals randomly ( well . . . what incentives do we have to seek pleasure ? ) 2 . our brains releases ever increasing quantities of pleasure chemicals ( well . . . one tiny nudge towards pleasure and we are soon fucked , i think ) . so , tipsy , or that level of high before the crash , can never last . nothing ever lasts . because our brain adjusts to stimulus over time , we seek new experiences and stay alive . but on the negative side to get " that feeling " we need more and more and , over time , the smell of her and her smile , might just not be enough .

your heart rate eliminating emotional anxiety and in fact often making you feel good emotionally thats why depressants see so much abusein the form of alcohol marijuana barbiturates benzodiazepines & gt ; functional tolerance & gt ; humans and animals develop tolerance when their brain functions adapt to compensate for the disruption caused by alcohol in both their behavior and their bodily functions . this adaptation is called functional tolerance ( 2 ) . * * chronic heavy drinkers display functional tolerance when they show few obvious signs of intoxication even at high blood alcohol concentrations ( bac ' s ) , which in others would be incapacitating or even fatal * * ( 3 ) . because the drinker does not experience significant behavioral impairment as a result of drinking , tolerance may facilitate the consumption of increasing amounts of alcohol . this can result in physical dependence and alcohol - related organ damage . without attracting much attention  if you have a 20 ounce soda bottle though its not as easy to pour  the following may sound unhygenic but i dont give a shit  nothing is going to get in the way of my into the toilet and fill the rest with your alcohol  this method will allow you to pour about 400 ml into the soda bottle mixed in with the 200 ml of soda  if you feel very daring just pour out all the soda and put all your alcohol in there do not recommend if you are doing this with vodka in a coke bottle though that would look weird  the goal is to make it seem like you are drinking whatever it  if you are a non terrorist looking person or a female with a purse this shouldnt be problem if your really cheap since the smaller liquor bottles do cost more at the store i just save mine after so pot is medicinal in a few states ? as was alcohol during prohibition . it makes you feel good . and not just while you ' re drunk , either . alcohol has lasting affects which , when used responsibly , make people happier , nicer , more concentrated , and just better human beings , even when they ' re sober . sure , like any drug , it gets abused , but i think because it ' s legal and so widely available , the alcohol abuse is more recognized . no one talks about the alcohol benefits anymore because too many assholes are killing people in drunk driving crashes or punching people or destroying their bodies . but there are people who are functioning in this world because alcohol exists . it ' s used as a medicine , a painkiller , an antidepressant , a mood stabilizer . it is a drug , right ? uh . . . have you ever been around a functioning alcoholic ? like one who has been going for decades at that pace ? their tolerance is through the roof , a constant supply of alcohol merely keeps the shakes at bay . being buzzed or tipsy is a distant memory of simpler times before physical dependence . it ' s nothing to be proud of , but if james bond really did keep up his consumption nonstop he was likely functioning fine . alcohol does very different things to a true alcoholic than a weekend warrior . back then people would come home and pour a few old fashioneds , rob roy ' s ( funny name , pure booze ) , manhattans or a real martini , all real drinks were pure alcohol with no ' mixers ' ( vermouth 17 % , bib whiskey 50 % , bitters 44 % , shake it in a tumbler because you wouldn ' t want too much water getting in . ) getting " drunk " when you have acclimated to drinking a 8 or more doubles of those a night for a decade takes dedication and a lot of trips to the bathroom . my grandmother had stories that would drink a modern college kid under a table , and it wasn ' t considered alcoholism back then . . . or frighteningly even drunk driving as they drank * while * driving . then our drinks became a majority of lemonade or sprite or cola with a weak shot of jack or " doing a shot " of jager ( 35 % ) and people think they are " drinking " while our grandparents were knocking back filled tumblers or martini glasses ( 4 - 6 shots ) with a higher alcohol content than their ' manly ' shot .

i had the same problem a couple of years ago ( specifically , i went to the hospital for alcohol poisoning twice in three weeks ) . i realized three main things about the way * i * was drinking . i ' m not sure if they will be true for you too . 1 . i never turned down * any * alcohol . whenever someone offered me a shot , i took it . whenever my friend finished a beer , i would finish mine too . i realized that everyone else i know at times turns down shots . i just never had . none . and i had been drinking regularly for about two years at that point . 2 . i would always count my drinks , but i always measured relative to my maximum limit ( i . e . the most i had drank before ) . let ' s say i drank 15 drinks one night the weekend before and didn ' t black out . i would assume that i could do the same the next night . there are a ton of factors that determine whether you black out ( food consumption , sleep , illness , etc . ) . even if i can drink 15 drinks given optimal conditions , i can ' t do that if i only slept 3 hours the night before . 3 . this kind of follows from the last point , but i found that the * number one * factor in how drunk i would get on a certain number of drinks was the speed at which i took them . if i drink all day , i can handle 15 shots easily . i * can ' t * take 15 shots in an hour and expect to remember anything else that night . so , some people would tell you to keep a hard limit . some people might even tell you to quit drinking , because you won ' t be able to control it . i would just suggest being more conscious of the factors that are causing your black outs . realize how much and at what speed you can tolerate drinks and turn down a shot once in a while .

( if you want , you can make it so that if the other person drinks , you have to drink as well . but that ' s optional ) 9 = make a rhyme . pick a word . everyone has to pick a word that rhymes with it . if they take too long or repeat a word , then that person drinks . 10 = never have i ever . everyone holds up 3 fingers . everyone goes around saying something they have never done . if someone in the circle has done it , they put a finger down . first one to run out of fingers must drink . if more than one run out , then all who do must drink . jack = categories . pick a category . people must name something in that category . if they say something that doesn ' t fit , repeat something , or take too long , they must drink . queen = question master . this person is question master . if they ask player a . question , they must respond in a question . if player does not , they must drink . king = make a rule . make up a rule . if someone breaks it , they must drink . popular rules are no cursing , little green man ( pretend there is a little green man on your cup . before drinking , you must take him off , drink , then put him back on . if you do not , you t drink again . some people go even further and say you have to finish the drink if you forgot . ) , ace = waterfall . person drawing card starts drinking and everyone else starts as well . go around in a circle . the person in front of yo must stop drinking before you can stop drinking . people have different rules and such . this happens to be the way i play it with my friends . it really is a fun game though .

sec . 121 . 575 — alcoholic beverages . ( a ) no person may drink any alcoholic beverage aboard an aircraft unless the certificate holder operating the aircraft has served that beverage to him . ( b ) no certificate holder may serve any alcoholic beverage to any person aboard any of its aircraft who— ( 1 ) appears to be intoxicated ; ( 2 ) is escorting a person or being escorted in accordance with 49 cfr 1544 . 221 ; or ( 3 ) has a deadly or dangerous weapon accessible to him while aboard the aircraft in accordance with 49 cfr 1544 . 219 , 1544 . 221 , or 1544 . 223 . ( c ) no certificate holder may allow any person to board any of its aircraft if that person appears to be intoxicated . ( d ) each certificate holder shall , within five days after the incident , report to the administrator the refusal of any person to comply with paragraph ( a ) of this section , or of any disturbance caused by a person who appears to be intoxicated aboard any of its aircraft . i dont drink nearly as much as i used to  now adays i have to deal with the exponentially worsening hangovers the increasing intellectual demands of my career beginning medical school in 2 weeks and the fact that i now spend most of my time living in an area that requires driving all the time  in that case i cant binge drink 5 6 7 8 or 9 drinks that i used to pretty regularly on the weekends and often during the week  on one hand i look back and part of me is taken aback by my drinking patterns  how did i accomplish so much in my late teenagers years and early adulthood life being so drunk so frequently  since i was a freshman in college binge drinking was just a normal part of my life for better or for worse  on one hand i am shocked by the lifestyle that i lived from the ages of 18 to 24  there were friendships i forever damaged times of intense social and personal humiliation that resulted in loss of social capital and relationships i permanently damaged because of my behavior while drunk  im sure i also stressed my physical and cognitive capacities due to drinking  i could always tell that my reading comprehension and working memory processing were affected after a night of heavy drinking and often for a few days afterwards  when youre heavy drinking every other day or every few days that mental fog adds up  also i tend to joke but seriously that the best way to lose weight is to simply stop drinking alcohol  on the other hand i realize that so many of the best things to happen in my life during that time were situations that came up people i met or decisions i made while i was and because i was drunk  ive met some of the most important loves of my life thus far while drunk and theres been countless friendships ive rekindled sometimes leading to romantic flings because i got drunk  theres been awful life situations that i only had the courage and intellectual brashness to break out of because was drunk and often intensely caffeinated  also theres life goals that i set formulated and pulled off because drunk me is a complete force of nature that can see the solution and the light at the end of any tunnel  in fact this brings me to the point of my postso many of my important individually defining moments and experiences both during college and the few years afterwards in new york city were while i was drunk  in fact i find that its only when im drunk or at least strongly buzzed that i can really remember those times and recount all the details how i felt and relate with them as if they are my own memories  when im sober its as if those memories are locked away with another of myself  i get drunk now and i start thinking wow so now i remember my life story and where i came from  i love the life i have been able to live and im fortunate to be where i am  however sometimes i feel that the life path and long term direction that sober me gets to live is largely the work of the intense highly decisive aggressive drunk me  as im not drinking too often nor too much nowadays i feel satisfied that i did my heavy drinking when i did in my life  although im not particularly old theres no way i could physically handle that level of alcohol intake and stay completely physically and cognitively functional to my fullest capacity especially considering the demands and responsibility of my career path as a physician  also despite the high costs the positive life long benefits heavy drinking during that time in life left me with outway them  everything turned out just fine anyways and frankly all those times i embarrassed myself for doing stupid stuff when i was an idiot underage drinking at college ended up not having any effect on my later life  all the people who were meant to be life long friends stayed with me always and all the people who were basically just my partydrinking buddies faded away as they would have anyways  all this being said i sometimes enjoy getting buzzed and remembering all those crazy adventures wacky brainstorming sessions and wild house parties i went to when i was really forging my own identity and becoming the person i am today living the life i am today

contrary to popular belief , pirates were not constantly drunk on rum . it was actually a maroonable offence to be drunk on the job . the image of pirates drinking rum non - stop does have some basis in reality , though . pirates typically drank a low - alcohol mixture called grog that was composed of low abv rum , water , and lime juice . grog was usually safer to drink than water sources they ' d find because the alcohol would purify the water . the lime juice was in there for flavour and to help stave off scurvy .

some of this is incorrect . for the purposes of getting drunk the liver does not care what type of alcohol you drink or what it is mixed with . ( the liver may coincidentally interact with the various organic compounds that lend different types of alcohol their flavor , but any alcoholic beverage is by far composed of water and alcohol more than any organic compound that lends flavor . ) in fact ethanol detoxification is a classic example of 0 - order kinetics . your liver will process the alcohol at the same rate , regardless of how much you ' ve had . that ' s why the 1 drink per hour rule exists , because that turns out to be about how much alcohol your liver can convert to aldehyde at once . also , alcohol absorption into your blood stream starts the second it enters your mouth , it definitely does not need to wait until the small intestine ; it gets absorbed all through the gi tract ( most is actually gone after the first part of the small intestine ) .

alcohol doesn ' t actually kill neurons . the most recent research i ' ve read indicates that normal alcohol consumption will numb or paralyze neurons for a short period of time ( leading to an actual increase in neuronal activity post - recovery , above baseline ) . as to the " slowest brain cells " , the variety of neurons and ganglion cells we have fire at different rates dependent upon their location with the brain ( not necessarily dependent , but associated to ) . but with respect to the inference that there ' s a correlation between drinking and feeling smart , technically , you will have greater neuronal performance during a recovery period after you ' ve been drinking . so while you ' re drinking , you ' re probably less intelligent ( numbed neurons ) , but post - hangover when neurons are " waking up " , you ' re most likely going to be in a better state intellectually . as with almost anything neuroscience related , this is all hypotheses on the basis of research . : - ) edit : still really drunk .

drinking at a party and drinking slowly ( yes , a beer an hour is fucking slow ) are two completely different animals . depending on your tolerance and metabolism , you might not even get past a mild buzz until possibly the next day . think about it . let ' s say a party starts at 10 and goes until 2 ( seems like a reasonable benchmark ) . during the course of these 4 hours you drink 10 beers . 10 / 4 = 5 / 2 = an average of 2 . 5 beers an hour . since you ' re drinking a beer an hour , drinking the same amount of beer during your two day " bender " will take you 10 hours . you ' re going to notice a significant difference . at least shoot for 1 . 5 beers an hour ( one beer every 40 minutes ) . anyway , now that i ' ve mathed , it ' s off to drink .

« [ what is alcoholic neuropathy ] ( http : / / www . healthline . com / health / alcoholism / alcoholic - neuropathy ) ? alcohol can be toxic to nerve tissue . people who drink too much may start to feel pain and tingling in their limbs . this is known as alcoholic neuropathy . in people with alcoholic neuropathy , the peripheral nerves have been damaged by too much alcohol use . the peripheral nerves transmit signals between the body , the spinal cord , and the brain . thiamine , folate , niacin , vitamins b6 and b12 , and vitamin e are all needed for proper nerve function . drinking too much can alter levels of these nutrients and affect the spread of alcoholic neuropathy . fortunately , abstaining from alcohol can help restore your nutritional health . this may improve your symptoms and help prevent further nerve damage . however , some alcohol - induced nerve damage is permanent . »

unlike my first time smoking pot , which was extensively premeditated over the course of several weeks , my first time getting drunk was completely spontaneous . it was some time around tenth grade . my friend and i were spending the night at my other friend ' s house watching south park , as we often did . some time in the early hours of the next morning , everyone had fallen asleep - my two friends and the parents - except for me . his parents had an absolutely monumental collection of booze , and it was all laid out in the sunroom on tables . i think they had recently hosted a get together . there were easily thirty different bottles of every kind of liquor one can imagine . at first i decided to grab a can of dr . pepper , sip a little bit off the top , and add some captain morgan ' s . the taste was a little strong since it mostly settled at the top of the can , but i quickly felt something click in my head . it was my first time feling what i know call a " buzz " , and it was great . i then proceeded to start swilling from the different bottles indiscriminately . i remember grey goose , some french vodka , and one that tasted very sweet and syrupy . that one could have been a mixer for all i knew . eventually i decided to go sit down and watch some more south park . i fell in the kitchen and just laid there on my face for a while enjoying the strange sensations . after some time , i made it to the chair . i remember tipping my head back and forth and having way too much fun doing it . i was so off balance it was like tossing it back and forth . it was pretty cool .

from a substance abuse professional ( no , not a professional drunk , i ' m a counselor ) , let me explain the real purposes behind these questionnaires . they are not designed to diagnose abuse or dependence , nor to be the basis for any treatment . they serve two purposes : 1 ) to help medical professionals to provide brief interventions with patients ; 2 ) to give people a chance to critically think about their substance use . on the first point , the medical community has a lot of pressure to treat problems at the lowest level possible . general doctors are usually the first medical professional that a patient sees ( and may be the only one they interact with for some time . ) by using these questionnaires , doctors are able to determine if substance use may be an issue with their patient . this may be necessary to decide on the best course of treatment for a particular issue . for example , elevated liver function tests may be caused by excessive alcohol use . a doctor needs to rule this out in order to address the liver problems . also , there are many medications that are specifically metabolized by the liver and it is necessary to monitor liver health . the second point is simply a chance for someone to stop and think objectively about their alcohol and drug use . the questionnaire does not say that if you can answer yes , then you are an alcoholic . it does , however , say that your alcohol and drug use might be problematic . when you ' re drinking , you may not always be able to be objective enough with the consequences of your actions . let ' s face it , we tend to justify our actions all the time , even when we know on some level that we are causing problems in our lives . if taking the questionnaire does cause you to stop and seriously consider your substance use , then it did its job . anyway , in the end , it doesn ' t matter what any questionnaire or doctor says . until someone accepts the real possibility that their substance use is causing parts of their life to be unacceptable , then nothing will change .

* shameless plug * i wrote a blog post about this . here it is : rule 2 : eat something . not to water down your drunkenness , because who wants that ? nor is it to have something to puke out , which is helpful , but it’s for a more important reason than that . hangovers . i’m not talking about hangovers where you have a huge headache or feel nauseous for the rest of the day . those are tolerable . i call these sorts of hangovers type 1 hangovers . there’s another kind of hangover that transcends type 1 , which is type 2 . i don’t know if anyone else experiences this , but this will happen to me if i have more than 750ml of liquor , give or take . it’s uncontrollable anxiety . so much so that once you’re done passing out , you wake up a few hours later , still sort of drunk , sort of hungover , and as previously stated , uncontrollable anxiety . and of course , unable to sleep . and it’s not about anything in particular . this has happened to me whether i’ve had work later in the day , nothing to do in the day , it’s even happened on a day where i was going to have a birthday dinner . i’ve been tinkering with ways to avoid type 2 , and so far i find eating a meal while drunk will usually offset this . it can be difficult to do so as an alcoholic , because you want to wait until you’re starving , and any slight hunger you replace with a drink or two , and by the time you’re starving you can barely stand . if you do find yourself in a type 2 , the only remedy / remedies i have found are to wait it out , to eat something , or to take sleeping pills . waiting it out can be a little excruciating , so try to keep yourself busy the best way you can ; tv , quick walk , something that will distract you . eating is good , but it won’t completely take it away , and eating can be difficult as the anxiety is great enough to make you not have an appetite . sleeping pills are the quickest way to get rid of it . however this may not always be an option you can take , as you might have work or other engagements in the day you can’t exactly fall asleep in the middle of . for me , it takes me about 2 - 3 to calm me down enough to sleep and be refreshed . disclaimer : taking the sleeping pills while experiencing a type 2 will produce a psychedelic - like trip . nothing very strong , but your thoughts will be meshed , and you might see those trademark holographic psychedelic colors , however it won’t be very strong . that concludes class for today . homework is to drink a glass of whiskey , preferably bourbon .

best advice i can give seems counter - intuitive at first , but . . . always drink on an empty stomach . it takes less booze to get you drunk , which is friendlier on your wallet . you get drunk faster , which is the whole point of this game , right ? but the best part is that you ultimately have less booze in your system . when you go to bed , you ' re not still slowly releasing booze reserves from your stomach to small intestines ( where 99 % of absorption happens ) . which means you ' re not maintaining a drunkenness during sleep , which means much less hangover and a faster recovery time . tl : dr - it sounds crazy , but if you plan on drinking , don ' t eat until the end of the night . thank me later .

1 . * 1 . 5oz whiskey x 40 % alcohol content = 0 . 6oz ethanol * 12oz beer x 5 % alcohol content = 0 . 6oz ethanol * 5oz wine x 12 % alcohol content = 0 . 6oz ethanol shitty light beers have less alcohol , diesel - ass imperial beers have quite a lot more ( 10 , 12 , 15 , 18 % ! ) . 5 % is a pretty fair mean value ; consider sam adams boston lager at 4 . 9 % . unless you ' re talking about awful watery beers at 3 % or lower , the booze content isn ' t very different . i ' m not looking at calories independent of carbohydrate content . i ' m looking at the two big sources of calories in a drink : from carbohydrates ( sugars / starches ) in the solution , and ethanol . the ethanol calories will be roughly the same , drink to drink , per standard drink . 2 . a carbohydrate is a large biological molecule , or macromolecule , consisting of carbon ( c ) , hydrogen ( h ) , and oxygen ( o ) atoms , usually with a hydrogen : oxygen atom ratio of 2 : 1 ( as in water ) ; in other words , with the empirical formula cm ( h2o ) n ( where m could be different from n ) . the word derives from * hydration * ( h and o ) of * carbon * chains ( c . ) ethanol is c2h6o . it is a carbohydrate . so are sugars ( glucose , dextrose , sucrose , maltose , maltodextrose , etc ) and other polysaccharides ( like starches . ) neither whiskey nor beer is a carbohydrate ; both contain several kinds of carbs , and beer tends to contain much larger quantities . ethanol is oxidized to acetaldehyde by alcohol dehydrogenase enzymes ( in both the liver and stomach lining ) , converting nad + to nadh , which acts as an energy carrier and goes on to synthesize lipids and convert pyruvic acid to lactic acid , among other fun metabolic goodies . this process has a net caloric ( heat / energy - generating ) metabolic effect , like sugar metabolism . with all due respect , friend , this comes from years of studying physiology , metabolism , organic and biochemistry , not from watching youtube and reading websites about health .

the goverment owned liquor stores here in sweden use a [ system ] ( http : / / www . systembolaget . se / dryckeskunskap / vara - symboler / smakklockan / ) like this for every product ( beer , wine cider , spirits etc . ) that shows the character of the drink . for example , a red wine will have charts for fullness ( maybe richness would be a better translation ) , dryness and acidity and a beer will have charts for sweetness , bitterness and fullness . they also have symbols for food that goes with the drink as well as a description of the taste . also , all personnel go through extensive training and are offered free wine tasting programmes . people here give them a lot of shit for having inconvenient opening hours and somewhat high prices , but no one can blame them for being less than professional .

( 1 ) buzz . your skin has a tingle that you almost didn ' t notice , and your thoughts are a little slowed . this feels good , but your speech is still fine , and your motor control has diminished at an almost imperceptible degree . your eyes look a little more relaxed than normal ; socializing is the best here . ( 2 ) you can feel an increased buzz . you sense of balance is slightly distorted and it rarely effects how you travel , but your finer movements that require greater dexterity have diminished more . you can pull your shit together to have a decent conversation with your mother , unless she ' s dead . ( 3 ) this is the prime state to be in . you are officially " drunk " . the previous two levels were just a buzzes ; this is the real deal . you occasionally stumble , and you have varying degrees of impaired speech ( this is dependent upon the attention you allot to your speech ; some people can still talk fine during this stage . ) your vision is adequately blurred , but you can still watch arrested development . mind you , you ' ll need to re - watch these episodes because you missed some of the finer details . you remember almost all of the big details during this phase . you say a few things that are considered uncouth , but you don ' t generally ruin relationships with what you ' re willing to say during this level . “well ya see , norm , it’s like this… a herd of buffalo can only move as fast as the slowest buffalo . and when the herd is hunted , it is the slowest and weakest ones at the back that are killed first . this natural selection is good for the herd as a whole , because the general speed and health of the whole group keeps improving by the regular killing of the weakest members . in much the same way , the human brain can only operate as fast as the slowest brain cells . excessive intake of alcohol , as we know , kills brain cells . but naturally , it attacks the slowest and weakest brain cells first . in this way , regular consumption of beer eliminates the weaker brain cells , making the brain a faster and more efficient machine . that’s why you always feel smarter after a few beers . ” - cliff clavin , * cheers *

it ' s possible that taking something called dihydromyricetin ( dhm ) before going to sleep may help you . dhm blocks alcohol from binding to your gaba ( a ) receptors , preventing the release of gaba as well as blocking some of the side effects of intoxication , such as slurred speech , uncoordination , etc . if these problems you are having are caused by how your body reacts to alcohol binding to gaba ( a ) receptors , dhm would definitely help . it ' s worth a shot . it ' s sold as a hangover prevention ( it prevents hangovers by fast metabolizing acetaldehyde ( hangover chemical ) in the blood and liver while you sleep , allowing you to wake and feel normal . ) you can get samples from a company called sobrup - they ' re on facebook and ebay .

i realize i am late here , but a little extra advice never hurt anyone . tolerance is only learned through trial and error . better to start slow and gradually work your way up . or if you are going to go balls deep right out of the gate then just make sure you have someone to keep an eye on you so that you don ' t kill yourself . the objective is to have fun , not injure yourself or others . if you have never ever been drunk before , simply go easy and don ' t just sit around drinking . you can be sitting on a stool , or a couch for a long time drinking and you won ' t really feel the true affects until you stand up and try to walk . many good men have met the floor very quickly because of this fact . also try to remember this fact : the cheaper the booze the worse you will feel the next day , and usually the worse it tastes . i realize college students may not have money to spend on good stuff , but you get what you pay for in most cases . as has already been stated , beer is an obvious good beginner choice , preferably a decent one . miller lite / coors light / bud light are the pretty normal staples that you will find at any bar / convenient . i would stay away from natty , key or stuff that is that cheap . if you have a few extra bucks you can try labatt blue , molson canadian , landshark , etc . if you really enjoy beer , then variety packs are always a good investment because you can learn what styles you like and don ' t . if you don ' t like beer , then there is the staples of vodka / mixers . if you are mixing these yourself , or at a house party situation and someone else is mixing , mind how much spirit is being poured . a solo cup of half vodka / half sprite ( or whatever your mixer ) is going to impact the number of drinks compared to a standard 1 . 5 / 2oz pour . be careful with these simply because you may not realize you are drinking it too fast until it is too late . vodka / sprite , vodka / tonic are good choices if you don ' t like the sweeter drinks . if you prefer sweeter then vodka / cran / sprite or pretty much any flavored vodka / and corresponding mixers . vodka / redbull usually puts me into a good place , but this is something that you should wait until you actually have some experience with because the added caffeine jolt can really mess with you . another good mixed drink choice is gin / tonic . if you like a bit sweeter drinks , i introduce a buddy of mine to a drink called a gimlet and he absolutely loved it . if you do this , some bartenders use vodka , but for a gimlet i prefer gin . personally i like whiskey , bourbon , rye or irish but made in cocktails ( i . e . old fashioned , manhattan , or good old whiskey / soda ) or on the rocks and sipping it . again this works best with semi - decent quality stuff . honestly though , if you are a novice i wouldn ' t go straight to whiskey . whiskey has a tendency to be a cruel bitch to those who don ' t know how to handle it . either way , good luck and enjoy . cheers !

cacaw—my family plays this one at get togethers . the drinking is based on behavioural tics of other people . a " council " decides at the beginning of the evening what behavioural tics will trigger drinking ( whoever is playing must be included , and non - players can listen in if they want ; the big rule is to make sure the targets don ' t know they ' re the targets ) . whenever a player notices a tic that was agreed on as a trigger , they shout " cacaw ! " , kind of like a crow . everyone playing must then drink ( the penalty for not drinking is usually drink double , but that can obviously be changed ) . after a few instances , most people figure out that they ' re being cacawed . once someone catches on they can either carry on as normal , or make a guess as to what they ' re being cacawed for . if they get it right , all players drain their drinks and that tic is no longer in play . it ' s a fun game and pretty simple , i hope i didn ' t make it too confusing .

no . see [ here ] ( http : / / www . healthcare - online . org / sugar - in - alcohol . html ) . all of the starches are converted to alcohol in the fermentation process for pure spirits . that which is not pure alcohol is almost all water ( in the case of whisky , esters , aldehydes , acids , and some other crap give it a characteristic flavour ) . another good article that goes into the specific chemistry can be found [ here ] ( https : / / www . whisky . com / information / knowledge / production / details / from - the - grain - to - alcohol . html ) . & gt ; this process either lasts until all sugar is used up ( typical for whisky ) or until the alcohol content has risen so far that the yeasts kill themselves off through their own products ( typical for wine with residual sweetness ) . calories in straight spirits therefore come from the alcohol itself . alcohol * does not * break down in your body to sugars - - your body just doesn ' t have a pathway for it . this also means that alcohol cannot ultimately be stored as fat . what happens , though , is that your body converts the alcohol to atp which your body preferentially uses as energy over current fat stores - - alcohol sure as hell won ' t make you slimmer . obviously if you are using mixers they will contain whatever sugars they contain and can greatly increase caloric intake and therefore convert to fat . beer and wine do not completely convert all of the sugars and may directly convert to fat .

also , are you looking for a buzz or to get drunk ? two different things . for a 16 year old who doesn ' t really drink , ~ 6 drinks in an hour will get you decently drunk ( a drink is considered a shot , a 12 oz beer , or 5 oz of wine ) . carbonation will cause you to get drunk faster ( carbonation speeds up the process of absorbing the alcohol into your bloodstream ) but it makes it taste far better than straight alcohol . i don ' t know if you ' re afraid of getting serious alcohol poisoning or just throwing up . your stomach cannot physically hold enough beer for you to die from alcohol poisoning . you would vomit multiple times before your bac is high enough to kill you since the water in the beer will fill you up . hard liquor is far more concentrated ( hence the " hard " ) . if you drink too much vodka or rum , for example , your body ' s natural defenses against alcohol poisoning ( vomiting actually saves your life as well as embarrassing you in front of your friends . ) don ' t have as much time to rid your stomach of the alcohol . so , i typically mix liquor with other liquids to prevent my drunken self from getting too ballsy and taking shot after shot . in the realm of hangovers , the main problem is dehydration . i usually buy myself a large gatorade to drink before i go to bed ( or some other sport drink that replenishes electrolytes ) . don ' t be an idiot , don ' t be afraid to call someone if you or one of your friends is unresponsive . are they aware and awake ? make sure to wake them up if they don ' t seem too hot . i know most towns and hospitals have mercy rules in place . if you bring in or call about someone who is underage and suffering from alcohol poisoning , whether you yourself are underage , you will not get in legal trouble . the authorities are interested in your friend ' s well being , so they don ' t want people getting afraid and having a friend die because they didn ' t call anyone .

i ' m not an expert , but my understanding is that higher quality alcohol ( specifically liquors , which are distilled ) undergoes more distillation in order to remove a lot of the " crap " , the toxins , that are in crude alcohol . a really cheap vodka might be distilled only once , so it would still have some of the bad stuff in it that causes worse hangovers , whereas a nice vodka ( grey goose ) might be distilled ten times and have a much , much smaller concentration of those toxic compounds . a hangover isn ' t caused purely by the chemicals in liquor besides alcohol , but higher concentrations of those chemicals cause worse hangovers and more adverse effects . edit : i welcome any corrections or additions to my statement from people more knowledgeable than i . i ' m just speaking from what little i have learned about the relationship between alcohol quality and hangovers .

i went through a seemingly similar breakup a little over a year ago . it still hurts sometimes . that ' s probably not what you want to hear , but it ' s true . everyone is different however , so maybe it won ' t take as long for you . the one thing that is certain is it will get better , so just keep that in mind . only advice i can give is what ' s worked for me in the past : don ' t stay friends , at least not right now . you both need to be apart to process things and heal . it ' s good that you ' re talking things out as you want to get closure , just don ' t draw it out or seek him out just because you ' re hurting - it wont help . do hang out with your friends and family as much as you can bear . i know the last thing you probably want to do is be out , but just try . pretty soon you ' ll have moments where you ' re out with friends and you realize you aren ' t thinking about him or at least the pain isn ' t as all consuming as it had been , and then that will start to stick around longer and longer . don ' t drink way too much , at least not consistently . alcohol is a major depressant , and after a big binge you ' re going to feel emotionally depleted and that will be coupled with the pain you ' re already in , but you probably won ' t be able to distinguish the two so you ' ll just feel awful . that being said , have some drinks and wallow a bit - you deserve to . it ' s a shitty situation and there ' s no point in trying to look at the bright side - yet . get off of tinder . it won ' t do anything for your self - esteem and you don ' t need any validation from some random dude - know that . there are guys out there that will take advantage of your desperation ( i ' m not trying to be mean , but you are desperate right now . it ' s to be expected ) and will use you and make you feel like shit again . i know from experience - girls do it too . focus on yourself . this goes along with not keeping in contact with your ex . chances are there are things you ' ve been wanting to do or are interested in that you were holding back on because you were in a committed relationship . this is an awesome opportunity for you to do whatever the fuck you want to do and not worry about anyone else . you ' ll also learn about yourself and realize a ) he is a fucking idiot for leaving you and didn ' t deserve you in the first place or b ) he totally sucked and you guys weren ' t right for each other at all and he saved you a lot of time and trouble ( or both ! ) . lastly , i want to say 28 is not old at all . 35 is the age where there is a statistically significant increase in the likelihood of complications during pregnancy and developmental disorders , and it ' s not like its guaranteed after 35 even . don ' t stress about that or feel like the clock is ticking - the last thing you want to do is rush into something . take time for and be good to yourself , it ultimately is for the better ( as much as you might not believe it right now ) . i hope at least some of this might be helpful . good luck with everything : )

1 . don ' t drink sugary drinks . people tell you not to drink different kinds of alcohol in a night but that ' s mostly bullshit . just stay away from sugary things and you ' re far less likely to feel shitty . " chick drinks " like cosmos , champagne , mixing with coca - cola and other sodas too much , jager , soco , schnapps , etc . , etc . , are all far more likely to render you a piece of shit the next day than drinking beer , wine , or straight liquor . 2 . drink water / gatorade . this is a lot easier to do and better for your hangover if you can do it while you ' re drinking . add an emergen - c to it , or just take some vitamin c . grapefruit / orange juice is also good , but if you ' re mixing it with your drinks too much you run the risk of drinking too much sugar ( once i drank a bottle of red wine and then a fifth of vodka mixed with grapefruit juice the whole way down ; had to vomit bile the next day ) . as a rule , if you can get even half a glass of water down for every drink you have , i think a really bad hangover is nigh impossible . 2a . the truth is there is a lot of water in beer . granted tolerance varies across individuals , in general only liquor is going to cause severe dehydration . it ' s not unmanly at all to ask for a glass of water with your bourbon . 2b . the last time i was really hungover it was because i went out dancing and got dehydrated . i don ' t want to say limit physical activity - we ' re all trying to have sex here - but when you ' re running around and yelling or dancing or whatever , you need to be extra careful to hydrate . 3 . for many people , smoking some pot in the morning can ease the feelings of nausea , physical pain , and immobility . it can definitely help you get some nutrition into yourself and make conscious decisions rather than lay in bed like a dead slug . 4 . ibuprofen ( advil ) . anyone who drinks regularly should generally avoid acetaminophen ( tylenol ) , since it is metabolized by the liver . since my hangovers often involve intense nasal congestion and sinus pressure , i also take pseudoephedrine ( sudafed ) when it ' s available . this can really help , but it ' s best not to take ibuprofen on an empty stomach if you can help it . 5 . depending on the person - don ' t force eggs and bacon down your throat if you ' re not feeling okay . have dry toast and water for breakfast , maybe some granola or cereal . simple is best . 6 . hair of the dog can help . there ' s a big difference between being hung over and waking up drunk . the latter can be a very fun experience . on many occasions , however , i have felt hangovers come on while i ' m still awake . it ' s best to keep in mind that you have hangovers in the morning because you ' re drinking at night and then sleeping - but depending on the circumstances , they can strike at any time . continuing to drink can postpone those effects and buy you time to apply other countermeasures . 7 . time and patience . a severe hangover can fuck you for days . don ' t think there are any magic tricks . just get your rest , avoid noise and bright light , and try not to drink too fuckin ' much . tl ; dr i drink alcohol

bio major here , breaking the seal is a real thing . when you drink , you block the reception of a hormone in your body called adh ( anti - diuretic hormone ) . the purpose of this hormone is to make your kidneys absorb water back out of your urine , since alcohol blocks the " station " that adh " docks in " , your body stops trying to conserve water , so you start pissing everything out . the reason it seems like you ' re pissing nonstop is because your body is continually pushing alcoholic beverages through as fast as possible because there is nothing nutritious to absorb . sincerely yours , drunk bio major .

chemically , they ' re all the same . there is no evidence to suggest that the psychoactive chemical in tequila is any different from that in red wine , for instance . however , there ' s a concept in drug theory known as ' set and setting , ' which theorizes that your mental state / mood ( set ) and immediate surroundings / people you ' re with ( setting ) affect your experience of a drug . while this is more obvious in something like a psychedelic , where a bad trip can easily occur if you enter the experience depressed or in a stressful environment , i can see how people associate different types of alcohol with different mental states . if you only drink tequila when you ' re out partying with friends and you only drink red wine when you ' re depressed and home alone , your lived experiences of the two different drinks will be markedly different .

" or compliment people , talk shit about people and say outrageous things . part of it comes from not thinking about it , and part of it comes from not caring . like this weekend , a heavily intoxicated badgernine told a friend who was visiting with his girlfriend that they could crash in my bed and have sex if they wanted to . i don ' t remember saying they could have sex in my bed . so both is the answer to that question . 5 ) ah drunken sex . . . . it ' s a little bit of both to be honest . due to inhibition being lowered , as well as vision being somewhat impaired , a man or woman who you might find bland turns into someone who is quite attractive that night , you don ' t care about what you say because you ' ve had ten servings of courage in a can so you attempt to initiate the hook up , annd it happens . or , when two people are interested in each other but haven ' t directly told each other , the two of them being drunk both end up going at it and having sex in what would have otherwise taken quite a bit longer . akward conversations ensue the next several days . hope that explained some of us to you ! remember , alcohol affects everybody differently and can bring out the inner demon or inner comedian in the person drinking .

running out of ideas to discuss for written academic works such as a term paper or custom essay is inevitable at times a lot of people make the mistake of assuming that a topic should be completely original and should not have been discussed before however ideas are limited and no one can assume that they are the first to discuss about a certain idea unless they invented it themselves nevertheless one can always find a new and refreshing way of discussing a usual topic for custom essays and the likean example of a favorite topic for academic writeups such as a custom essay is the issue of alcoholism many papers have discussed this topic in several approaches however this should not stop anyone from tackling this issue here are some suggested topics for the subject of alcoholism as well as unusual takes to pursue for the said topicdifferent drinking styles  people who develop alcoholism usually have different drinking styles and patterns from people who do not suffer from it discussing drinking styles in relation to alcoholism will enable people to understand the role of a persons drinking style and its possibility of becoming an alcoholic because of it taking this approach to alcoholism is a good way of setting a custom essay apart from othersdrinking customs of cultures around the world  alcoholism can also vary according to ones culture researching about different drinking customs and relating it to cases of alcoholism in different countries can help explain the reason behind such case of alcoholism through custom essaysalcoholism and its relation to religion  alcohol abuse is something mostly frowned upon by many people of different backgrounds and faiths however their degrees of alcohol tolerance vary from each religion or sect exploring this topic in connection to the issue can help in informing people about how each faith sees the role of alcohol in their livesthese suggested approaches are some of the topics that one can use when making a written academic work about alcoholism another way of finding unusual approaches for this subject is to look up related topics using online search engines or conventional research materials such as textbooks and encyclopedias

" i ' ll quit " is a mind state that has bit me in the butt way too many times , with alcohol and many other things . if i feel myself going off the deep end into a shitty routine what i do is set realistic goals on amount of time to stop drinking . say a week , several weeks , a month , or whatever . that way my body and mind can hit a reset but i don ' t feel the overwhelming pressure of " oh no i ' m never gonna drink again " . then at the end of the process i reevaluate what is most healthy for me and go from there . not sure if this ' ll work for you but it is something i ' ve done that i found has given me awareness of my relationship with alcohol .

there ' s some good ones at the link below http : / / en . wikipedia . org / wiki / blood _ alcohol _ content # highest _ recorded _ blood _ alcohol _ level . 2fcontent & gt ; highest recorded blood alcohol level / content there have been reported cases of blood alcohol content higher than 1 . 00 % . in march 2009 , a 45 - year - old man was admitted to the hospital in skierniewice , poland , after being struck by a car . the blood test showed blood alcohol content at 1 . 23 . the man survived but did not remember either the accident or the circumstances of his alcohol consumption . [ 64 ] one such case was reported by o ' neil , and others in 1984 . they report on a 30 - year - old man who survived a blood alcohol concentration of 1 , 500 mg / 100 ml blood after vigorous medical intervention . [ 65 ] in south africa , a man driving a mercedes - benz vito van containing 15 sheep , allegedly stolen from nearby farms , was arrested on december 22 , 2010 , near queenstown in eastern cape . his blood had an alcohol content of 1 . 6 g / 100 ml . also in the vehicle were five boys and a woman who were also arrested . [ 66 ] in 2004 , an unidentified taiwanese woman died of alcohol intoxication after immersion for twelve hours in a bathtub filled with 40 % ethanol . her blood alcohol content was 1 . 35 % . it was believed that she had immersed herself as a response to the sars epidemic . [ 67 ] in poland , a homeless man was found sleeping half - naked on january 28 , 2011 , in cieszyn . his blood had an alcohol level of 1 . 024 % . despite the temperature of −10 °c and extremely high blood alcohol content the man survived . [ 68 ] in december 2004 , a man was admitted to the hospital in plovdiv , bulgaria , after being struck by a car . after detecting a strong alcohol odor , doctors at a hospital conducted a breath test which displayed the man ' s blood alcohol content at 0 . 914 . [ 69 ] the man was treated for serious injuries sustained in the crash and survived . [ 70 ] in february 2005 , french gendarmes from bourg - en - bresse , france , conducted a breath test on a man who had lost control of his car . he had an alcohol content of 0 . 976 . [ 71 ] he was not injured in the accident but was charged with a €150 fine and his driving license was canceled . in 1982 , a 24 - year - old woman was admitted to the ucla emergency room with a serum alcohol concentration of 1 . 5 ( 1 , 510 mg / dl ) , corresponding to a bac of 1 . 33 . she was alert and oriented to person and place . [ 72 ] serum alcohol concentration is not equal to nor calculated in the same way as blood alcohol content . [ 73 ] in 2012 , oct 26th a man from olszewo - borki community , poland , who died in a car accident , had 2 . 23 % ; however , the blood sample was collected from a wound and thus possibly contaminated . water : i keep a gallon of water next to my bed / in my fridge at all times . i always make sure to drink a ton of it before falling asleep and then again immediately after waking up . since doing so , i have found that hangovers are damn near non - existent . mostly due to the fact that hangovers are generally caused by dehydration . don ' t get me wrong , i still wake up once in a while with a pretty big buzz , but slam that water and then this is where work comes in . work : still pounding water and now working my arse off ( or working out if you don ' t have a physical job ) , i find that my buzz wares , but i don ' t get that super shitty feeling . you know , when you go from drunk to hungover with no sleep involved . worst . transition . ever . another one i use is training yourself for a binge . while not advised , there are things you can do to train yourself for your ultra - dumb - drunk moments . things i ' ve trained myself to do : taking pictures every 30 minutes ( set a notification on your phone ) while out drinking . helps piece together those blackouts . being creative . that drunk poetry thing i posted . . . after a while doing that , i realized keeping my brain thinking in a way that involved some form of creativity , helped me focus more , fighting off blackouts and just idiotic moments . it ' s ok to go to a bar by yourself . become a regular , make friends with the staff . i have friends that bitch about how much they spend at the bar constantly . i go to my regular bar . . . i spend 20 dollars and drink like a sailor . don ' t mix your liquors . generally leads to the worst hangovers . do shit around your home ! this one , i recently tried and it has worked out pretty well . when i come home , i just start cleaning and organizing stuff . the last time i got completely bombed , i came home and pretty much cleaned my place top to bottom . my sober / hungover self . . . had many thanks to my drunk self . this is all i ' ve got for now .

this is true for most people . the body absorbs and burns off alcohol much more slowly than most people realize ; if you chug one beer , it probably won ' t be absorbed for about an hour , and the body is really only capable of burning off about one drink ' s worth of booze per hour . so if you ' re having two or three drinks an hour , the body will be absorbing more alcohol than it ' s burning off . . . thus the sudden spike . btw . . . this is how people get duis . they wait an hour after their last drink , not realizing that they ' ve actually been increasing their bac , not lowering it . so the main reasons why * * * on average * * * women get intoxicated faster and more efficiently than men is due to these biological factors : * women have a lower concentration of water than men . so after drinking same amount of alcohol as a man , a woman would have a higher blood alcohol concentration . * women have a lower concentration of the enzyme , alcohol dehydrogenase , than men . this enzyme metabolizes the alcohol in the gastrointestinal system before entering the bloodstream . less of the enzyme leads to more alcohol being absorbed into the bloodstream . * hormonal changes prior to menstruation can cause women to become intoxicated quicker as well .

alcohol is a diuretic . when you drink you have slightly more toxic substances in your bladder so less water is reabsorbed at the kidneys to allow you to dilute those slightly more toxic substances . after you break the seal there is no watery liquid already in the bladder for the toxic substances to be diluted in so the kidneys reabsorb less water , so your bladder fills faster with water to dilute the substances . this is also what causes hangovers , dehydration .
